name: The Langham, Sydney
positioning: Irish Georgian-style hotel on Kent Street in Millers Point, with an underground spa and a tennis court opposite
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet historic neighborhood base near Barangaroo, Walsh Bay and The Rocks
Guests who want a spa, a pool and a tennis court close by

facts.text: The hotel is on Kent Street in Millers Point, equidistant to Barangaroo, Walsh Bay and The Rocks.
The hotel is in an Irish Georgian-style building.
The hotel has a wall mural of Bondi Beach in the 90s.
The Observatory Suite has a grand dining room and views of Observatory Hill and the Sydney skyline.
Premier Terrace Rooms are on the third floor and have a balcony overlooking the city and Western Harbour.
The Residence is a two-bedroom, two-bathroom suite with a modern kitchenette and skyline views.
All rooms have a marble bathroom with double basins and a separate bath and shower.
Afternoon Tea in the Palm Court is served with Wedgwood tableware and can be paired with Champagne.
Bistro Remy serves breakfasts and dinners made with local produce.

highlights.text: The pool has a starry ceiling that is a painted replica of the Southern Hemisphere.
The Observatory Suite and Observatory Bar pay homage to the Sydney Observatory, which is just opposite the hotel.
The Day Spa by Chuan is underground and offers massages, body treatments and facials.
The hotel has a championship-size tennis court just opposite the hotel.
The Langham Pink Taxi, a rose-hued London cab, takes guests around the area free of charge for meetings, shopping and dining.

considerations.text: The Pampered Pets programme offers pet-sitting and dog-walking services for a fee.
An extra bed for a third guest is available on request in rooms with King or two double beds.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Langham, Sydney
